title: RookRail
wrapsNative: A column of icon buttons on the accent colour (Image(systemName:) in a Button with an accessibility label, a dot for something new), beside the page; MonarchAvatar for the account; the Help & support button opens a sheet; MonarchWorkspaceSwitcher and MonarchSpaceSwitcher inside rook-rail
summary: A recipe, not a component: Rook's primary navigation on iOS: the app's name, the workspace and space switchers, the Rook sections with unread counts, workspace links into Rook ID, Help & support and the account menu, in a sidebar that becomes the root list on iPhone.
whenToUse: As the top-level navigation of a Rook app with more destinations than fit a tab bar, so every Rook app is arranged the same way.
whenNotToUse: For apps outside Rook, or with five or fewer destinations, use the app-shell recipe (TabView, with .sidebarAdaptable from iOS 18). For navigation inside a section use NavigationStack and List.
api: NavigationSplitView { List(selection: $current) { Section { MonarchWorkspaceSwitcher(selection:workspaces:); MonarchSpaceSwitcher(selection:spaces:) } Section { ForEach(items) { item in NavigationLink(value: item.id) { Label(item.name, systemImage: item.systemImage) }.badge(item.unread) } } Section("Workspace") { Link(destination: url) { Label("Members", systemImage: …) }.accessibilityHint("Opens in Rook ID") } Section { Button { showsSupport = true } label: { Label("Help & support", systemImage: …) } } }.navigationTitle(appName).toolbar { ToolbarItem(placement: .primaryAction) { Menu { … } label: { MonarchAvatar(…, isDecorative: true) } } } } detail: { … }

options.name: app name
options.description: The Rook app's name as the sidebar's title.

options.name: switchers
options.description: At the top of the sidebar, in their own section.

options.name: sections
options.description: One row per destination with a decorative symbol, the selected state from List(selection:) and an unread count with badge(_:). Group destinations into Sections with headers when there are many.

options.name: workspace links
options.description: Members, billing and other Rook ID pages; they leave the app, so each has the hint "Opens in Rook ID".

options.name: support
options.description: Help & support, which opens the support-panel recipe in a sheet.

options.name: account
options.description: The account-menu recipe in the primary toolbar slot, labelled by a decorative MonarchAvatar.

states.name: iPhone
states.description: The sidebar is the root list; choosing a destination pushes it, and the back button returns to the list.

states.name: iPad and wide windows
states.description: The sidebar sits beside the detail; the system button collapses and shows it.

states.name: selected
states.description: The current destination has the system selection highlight and the selected trait.

states.name: unread
states.description: A count badge at the end of the row; a count of 0 shows nothing.

states.name: support open
states.description: The support-panel sheet at medium height, which can be pulled to large.

appearance: The system sidebar list and navigation bar, Monarch switchers and avatar, and the system badge. The theme's accent tints selection. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow the system and the Monarch theme roles.
platformNotes: The web RookRail is a 48-point rail of icons that expands to labels, remembers its state in the rook_rail cookie shared across Rook apps, and becomes a top bar with a drawer below 768 px. iOS has no navigation drawer; its pattern for many destinations is a sidebar, so the recipe uses NavigationSplitView: on iPhone the sidebar is the root list and destinations push, on iPad it sits beside the content and collapses with the system button. Android uses a modal navigation drawer for the same role. The cookie and the expanded state do not apply: each app restores its own destination (for example with SceneStorage). Keyboard shortcuts and tooltips of the collapsed rail are not offered; VoiceOver reads each row's label. Links to Rook ID and other products leave the app, so the web's "opens in a new tab" becomes the hint "Opens in Rook ID". The web's theme toggle and notifications slots go into the account menu and the toolbar (the identity-bar recipe). Rook-specific: apps outside Rook use the app-shell recipe.
accessibility: The sidebar's navigation title names the app and is read first.
Each destination is a standard navigation row read as its label; the selected one has the selected trait.
The unread count is a system badge, text rather than a colour; check on a device that VoiceOver reads it with the row.
Workspace links have the hint "Opens in Rook ID" so leaving the app is not a surprise.
The account menu is named "Account menu for …" and its avatar is decorative.
Rows and buttons are at least 44 points; symbols in labels are decorative.
edgeCases: Long app or destination names truncate in the sidebar title and wrap in rows at the largest text sizes.
With no spaces, MonarchSpaceSwitcher hides itself.
Restore the selected destination when the app relaunches; the web's shared cookie has no iOS counterpart.
Many destinations: group them in Sections with headers instead of one long list.
